function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieve the current weather conditions for a specified location in either Celsius or Fahrenheit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to retrieve the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the temperature.

function.name: search_local_docs
function.description: Searches the local knowledge base for documents that match the given natural language query and returns relevant document entries. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search query expressed in natural language, such as 'What are the symptoms of a cold?'.

limit.description: The maximum number of documents to return.

include_metadata.description: Determines whether to include metadata for the documents in the search results.

**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year** - **Film:** *Princess Mononoke* (Japanese title: *Mononoke Hime*) - **Year of award:** 1997 (20th Japan Academy Film Prize) *Princess Mononoke* was the first Ghibli feature to receive the top honor at the Japan Academy Awards, beating out other domestic contenders such as *Kimi no Na wa* (2016) and *Spirited Away* (2001) for that particular year. --- ### How its box‑office success boosted Ghibli’s international profile | Domestic impact | International impact | |-----------------|----------------------| | • Grossed ¥1.5 billion in Japan (≈ $12 million), becoming the highest‑grossing Japanese film of its time.
• Established Ghibli as a commercial powerhouse in Japan, giving the studio leverage in negotiations with distributors. | • Released in the U.S. by Walt Disney Studios in 1999 (under the “Disney–Ghibli” partnership).
• Earned $13 million worldwide, proving that a Japanese animated film could perform well in Western markets. | | • The film’s critical acclaim (winning Picture of the Year) reinforced its artistic credibility. | • The U.S. release introduced Ghibli’s storytelling style to a broad English‑speaking audience, sparking curiosity about other titles. | | • The success helped finance subsequent projects (e.g., *Spirited Away*, *Howl’s Moving Castle*). | • Disney’s involvement opened doors for future co‑distribution deals, eventually leading to Netflix acquiring streaming rights for Ghibli’s catalog. | | • The film’s popularity contributed to the opening of the Ghibli Museum in Mitaka (2005), further cementing the brand’s cultural presence. | • International fans began collecting Ghibli merchandise, creating a global fan‑base that supported later releases and merchandise sales. | **Bottom line:** *Princess Mononoke*’s box‑office triumph—both at home and abroad—proved that Studio Ghibli’s blend of lush animation, complex characters, and environmental themes resonated beyond Japan. This success convinced major distributors (first Disney, later Netflix and others) that Ghibli’s catalog was a valuable asset, leading to wider releases, higher budgets for future films, and a lasting international fan community.
